chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A woman has a husband, and he refuses to give her permission to perform Hajj, and she has not yet performed the Hajj of Islam (obligatory). Her husband was absent, and he had forbidden her from performing Hajj. He said: 'There is no obedience to him for her in the Hajj of Islam, and there is no need for his permission for her to perform Hajj if she wishes.'

key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْإِسْلَامِ: The first obligatory Hajj performed by a Muslim
key_terms.طَاعَة: Obedience (specifically to the husband in this context)

ai.seo_question: Does a wife need her husband's permission to perform the obligatory Hajj if he refuses to let her go?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a wife’s obedience to her husband is not absolute regarding the performance of Hajjat al-Islam, the obligatory pilgrimage. He establishes that she may perform it independently if she wishes, as the husband’s prohibition does not negate her religious duty, highlighting the precedence of divine obligation over spousal authority in this specific context.
